newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat closes lower on outlook for good crops.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat closes lower on outlook for good crops.

text.p: CBOT soft red winter wheat futures closed lower on outlooks for a good wheat production year in the U.S., traders said.
There have been few severe weather problems recently in the U.S. winter wheat and spring wheat growing regions which led to the ideas for abundant wheat yields.
Forecasts for showers this week in the drier areas of Kansas and Nebraska's hard red winter wheat areas continued to weigh on the market.
Also active seeding of the U.S. spring wheat crop led to ideas for a satisfactory year for spring wheat yields.
Wheat futures moved lower despite talk Egypt may be seeking 300,000 to 500,000 tonnes of wheat. U.S. exporters discounted that talk and said there were no signs Egypt was looking for more wheat soon.

USDA Thursday said Egypt bought 250,000 tonnes of U.S. soft red winter wheat which was a portion of the reported sale early this week of 400,000 tonnes to that country. Also there was news early Thursday that Pakistan was seeking 376,000 tonnes of U.S. or Australian white wheat.
Wheat futures closed 1/2 to five cents lower, with July down five at $3.77-1/4 a bushel.
Traders said USDA's weekly export sales report was neutral to supportive for wheat futures.

The government early Thursday said U.S. net wheat export sales during the week ended May 15 totaled 369,100 tonnes, combined old and new crop, which was near the high end of expectations for 300,000 to 400,000 tonnes.
Merrill Lynch Futures sold three million bushels of July and Prudential Securities sold 1.5 million bushels of July, traders said.
FIMAT Futures bought 2.5 million July, Cargill Inc bought 1.5 million July and Term Commodities bought one million bushels of July, traders said.
Wheat futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 16,000 contracts, above the 15,025 traded Wednesday.

In wheat options, Prudential Securities bought 400 July $4.00 calls at six to 6-1/2 cents and sold 400 September $4.40 calls at eight to 8-1/4 cents, traders said. Rand Financial bought 300 December $4.00 calls at 28 cents and sold 300 September $3.50 puts at six cents, traders said.
Wheat options volume was estimated at 8,500 contracts, above the 8,234 traded Wednesday.
